label: copy-phase input token i fed back (from 3rd output onward)
explanation: Token detector for the letter i, but only in the copy phase: it fires when the fed-back input is i (that is, the model just output an original i) and the step is far enough into the copy (recall_idx >= 3). It never fires during the original phase, on the delimiter, or on any input other than i. On copied i at recall_idx 1-2 it is mostly silent or very weak (lowest quartile), and the firing rate rises with position. Magnitude also grows with position: the top examples are i at recall_idx 6-7 in L=9 sequences, often the first of a repeated i i pair near the end, where the second i is weaker. Only first-occurrence inputs are affected trivially (copy-phase inputs are never first occurrences). The FPs are mostly early copied i at recall_idx 3 in short sequences.

issues: Main claims hold. Test scores reproduce: P 0.941, R 0.919, F1 0.930, mass recall 0.979. On dev, all activation is in the copy phase and on in_tok == i (rate 0.297, lift 32x). Original phase, delimiter and every other token are at exactly 0.

The recall_idx gradient is real. Firing rate is 0.0003 at recall_idx 1, 0.009 at 2, 0.026 at 3 and 0.033-0.034 at 4-8. The recall_idx==2 slice has precision 0.28 and holds only 2.1% of activation mass. Missed activations are weak (around 0.01-0.2 of max) copied i at recall_idx 1-2. That matches the claim that early copied i is mostly silent or in the lowest quartile.

Almost all false positives are at recall_idx==3, where precision is 0.80. At recall_idx>=4 precision is 0.996. Splitting recall_idx==3 by L, to_go, in_count, prev_tok or correct turns up no systematic pattern, so the residual looks like threshold noise at the onset.

Minor overclaim: the explanation says false positives come 'mostly in short sequences'. At recall_idx==3, precision is 0.84 for L<=5 and 0.78 for L>=7, so the false positives are not concentrated in short sequences.
The 'second i of an i i pair is weaker' claim is weakly supported. Precision is 0.86 when prev_tok==i, versus 0.94 overall. This slice is tiny (2.8% recall) and does not matter to the predicate.
Adding correct==1 or changing the handling of recall_idx 3 makes no measurable difference: F1 goes from 0.9300 to 0.9303. No better predicate was found.
